P1.evidence: The recording starts mid-frame, so any setter read-back would have preceded the file and cannot be scored. The visible portion of the frame is the usual reduced version — "Build out what it is that you want to achieve, and then if everything makes sense, we can talk about the coaching. If not, that's fine as well. Alrighty?" — with agreement given ("Got it, got it. Yep. Cool."). The open question ran in a stronger form than usual: "in your opinion, then, what's the biggest challenge you're facing right now in terms of your health and your fitness journey?"

P2.evidence: Diet was asked directly and answered in real detail — "what kind of stuff are you eating at the moment... what's your diet look like?" producing the full vegetarian picture, the sugar and wheat cuts, and the millet switch. Training was asked: "Are you doing any training whatsoever at the moment?" Weight was confirmed rather than asked ("And you weigh 90 kilos at the moment") after the prospect volunteered 5'11" and 90 kg; age was volunteered and never asked, which matters on this call because what he volunteered was that he is under thirty. Work was never asked — software engineering was volunteered. No health-conditions question and no injury question at all; the prospect happened to say "I don't have as such, like, you know, body aches or anything", which is luck rather than screening. No sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: The strongest goals work in the batch. The six-month question was asked cleanly ("Let's fast forward six months. What does that actually look like for you?") and produced belly fat, definition, and a target of 80 kg. The bridge was asked early and properly: "what's caused you to want that? What's, like, the motivation, the drive to be, like, hell yeah, I'm going to go for it." The rep then went one layer down — "Is that something that's important? Just feeling, you know, summertime comes, the tank top comes out, feeling confident, feeling your best. Is that really what you're going for?" — and got the real answer: confidence spilling into everything else, and the health-before-money line. Reflect-back landed: "It trickles into every area of your life, right?" — "Correct." Where it stopped short is the same place as every other call in this batch: 'who else does that impact' was never asked, so the wife doing the diet alongside him and the friends he wants to inspire stayed decorative rather than becoming the reason to buy.

P4.evidence: "What do you feel like is the biggest thing that's held you back so far? Because everything that we do is tailored and I want to make sure that a big thing for us is removing roadblocks for people." The prospect named the gap himself and named it twice: "maybe it's just a lack of structure" and "just swimming is not helping so maybe like a good structure." The rep also established that he had never had a coach and tested his readiness for one. Past attempts were only loosely mapped and the 'information isn't the problem' line was never run, although the prospect had set it up perfectly: "I try to follow certain things online which might work or not work."

P5.evidence: Not run. No two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The rep substituted a possibility frame for a consequence frame — "Honestly, I think you're in a beautiful spot, right?... You have the time. You have the commitment. You just need the structure" — which is warm and worked here, but it means the deal was carried entirely by the prospect's pre-existing motivation. On a call with a prospect who had already quit several self-directed attempts, the cost of the next failed attempt was never priced.

P6.evidence: The best-sequenced commitment work in the batch, even though the scripted questions were not used. Before presenting anything the rep secured the practical yes on capacity — "Are you ready to commit to three to four days a week, 30 to 45 minutes a day?" — and the yes on timing — "are you looking to, like, really start moving towards this goal now, or is it something that you're looking to do in a few months' time?" He also tested readiness for coaching: "Do you feel like you're ready for that, for the discipline?" What is missing is the belief question in its real form (does the prospect believe HE can get there with the right structure) and the all-in question entirely. The order was right; the questions were softer than the script.

P11.evidence: Steps 1 and 2 ran. Payment was structured and collection commenced live — tier chosen, two-payment split agreed, card type confirmed, and the rep moved to take details ("I want to make sure I get all your information correct. Let me just remove the recording"). Onboarding with Trevor was booked for Tuesday 26th at 1:15pm Eastern, deliberately scheduled before the house move so no time would be lost. Steps 3 and 4 were not run at all: no agreement email confirmed, nothing signed on the call, and no mention of the welcome email, the Skool community link or the onboarding questionnaire. The rep did handle equipment well (kettlebell weights to be specified by Trevor, plus a $20 door pull-up bar), which is not on the checklist but removes a real barrier.

objection_plays.detail: "I'm moving this week, so I would probably start something like this in the first week [of June]." The rep did not run the OD play and did not need to — he dissolved the objection structurally by separating the purchase from the start date: "your first day of the six months or the 12 months would be your first workout day, no you don't lose any time it just means that by the time you're ready everything's already ready." He then booked the onboarding before the move so Trevor's build time ran during the relocation. Scored partial because the outcome was achieved by good improvisation rather than by the play, and none of the scripted moves appeared.

Eligibility, raised by the prospect in his first answer and never picked up: "I'll be touching 30 in a couple of months. I know the coaching is for 30 and above, essentially." He believed there was an age floor, said so on the record, and the rep neither confirmed, corrected nor addressed it. There is no scripted handling for a prospect who volunteers that he may not qualify, and no visible policy on whether the floor exists. See the flags file.

Programme-fit question with no scripted path: "how much of a barrier you think would cause me being vegetarian? Is there any issues or it's all good?" The nutrition pillar as delivered on every call in this batch is built on red meat, eggs and dairy. The answer here was four words plus an aside — "As long as you hit your protein, you're fine" and "Trevor might recommend you eat more eggs" — from a rep who had just heard a detailed and competent vegetarian protein plan. The prospect accepted it, but the script has nothing for the dietary-fit objection and this is the second known gap category (clinical fit, dietary fit) where a rep is left improvising.

notes: The best-sequenced call in the batch: capacity and timing were both locked before the price, the timing conflict was dissolved rather than argued with, and the close was clean. Two things to fix. The consequence frame is still entirely absent, so a motivated buyer closed himself and a less motivated one would not have. And the two questions the prospect asked about whether he actually fits — under thirty, vegetarian — were each answered in a sentence or not at all.
